attractions.name: Victoria Falls, Zambia side
attractions.desc: The Zambian bank offers closer, wetter views of the falls, including the thrilling Knife-Edge Bridge walkway that puts visitors right beside the plunging water. In the dry season, the seasonal Devil's Pool allows swimming at the very edge of the falls. It pairs naturally with the wider views available from the Zimbabwean side.

attractions.name: South Luangwa National Park
attractions.desc: Widely credited as the birthplace of the walking safari, this park offers close, guide-led encounters with leopards, elephants, and hippos along the Luangwa River. Its density of wildlife rivals much larger, more famous parks, but with far fewer vehicles. Night drives here are also well regarded for spotting nocturnal species.

attractions.name: Lower Zambezi National Park
attractions.desc: A riverside park facing Zimbabwe's Mana Pools across the Zambezi, known for canoe safaris that glide silently past elephants and hippos at the water's edge. Its combination of river-based and land-based game viewing sets it apart from more standard drive-only parks. It's less developed than South Luangwa, appealing to travelers wanting a quieter alternative.

attractions.name: Kafue National Park
attractions.desc: One of the largest national parks in Africa, though still relatively undeveloped for tourism, offering a real sense of wilderness. Its size supports diverse habitats, from open plains to dense woodland, with strong populations of lion, leopard, and antelope species found nowhere else in the region. Access requires more planning than the more established parks.

attractions.name: Livingstone town
attractions.desc: The town nearest Victoria Falls, named after the explorer David Livingstone, functions as the country's adventure tourism hub. Bungee jumping, white-water rafting, and microlight flights over the falls are all organized from here. The Livingstone Museum offers useful context on the region's colonial and pre-colonial history.

attractions.name: Lake Kariba, Zambian shore
attractions.desc: Zambia's side of this vast man-made lake offers houseboat trips and lakeside lodges with wildlife viewing along the shoreline. It's a slower-paced counterpoint to the more intense safari parks, with fishing and sunset cruises as the main activities. The lake also borders Zimbabwe, and cross-border trips are common.

itinerary.label: Days 1–2
itinerary.title: Livingstone & Victoria Falls
itinerary.desc: Close-up views of the falls plus optional adventure activities in town.
itinerary.cost: Victoria Falls National Park entry costs about $20 for foreigners; adventure activities (bungee, white-water rafting) run $100–160 each.
itinerary.food: Try nshima with a local relish at a Livingstone restaurant for an accessible introduction to Zambian home cooking.

itinerary.label: Days 3–5
itinerary.title: South Luangwa
itinerary.desc: Walking safaris and night drives through one of Africa's most wildlife-dense parks.
itinerary.cost: Park fees and walking safari costs are typically bundled into camp packages, roughly $400–700+/night all-inclusive.
itinerary.food: Meals are included at almost every South Luangwa camp, often featuring fresh local produce.

itinerary.label: Days 6–7
itinerary.title: Lower Zambezi
itinerary.desc: Canoe safaris along the river, gliding past elephants and hippos.
itinerary.cost: Similarly bundled into all-inclusive camp rates, given the park's remoteness.
itinerary.food: A sundowner drink during an evening canoe safari is a genuine Lower Zambezi tradition.

itinerary.label: Day 8
itinerary.title: Lusaka
itinerary.desc: A short stop in the capital before departure.
itinerary.logistics: ~4h drive or short flight from Lower Zambezi
itinerary.food: Grab a final Zambian meal at a Lusaka restaurant before your onward flight.

goodToKnow.tipping: USD 10–15/day for safari guides is standard
goodToKnow.safety: Tourist areas are safe and well organized; most travel is guided
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Domestic flights connect Livingstone with the safari parks; roads to remote parks can be very slow
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Livingstone's Harry Mwanga Nkumbula International Airport (LVI) is the natural start for this route, right by Victoria Falls

food.name: Nshima
food.desc: A thick maize porridge and Zambia's staple food, eaten with a meat or vegetable relish.

food.name: Kapenta
food.desc: Small dried or fresh fish from Lake Kariba, a common protein source.

food.name: Ifisashi
food.desc: Vegetables cooked in a rich groundnut (peanut) sauce.

food.name: Munkoyo
food.desc: A fermented, slightly sweet traditional drink made from maize and munkoyo root.

faq.q: Do I need a visa for Zambia?
faq.a: Yes, a visa on arrival is available for most nationalities, including the KAZA Univisa, which also covers neighboring Zimbabwe and cross-border day trips to Botswana.

faq.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Livingstone (LVI), right by Victoria Falls and the natural start for this route.
A single visa (about $50) covering both Zambia and Zimbabwe, useful if you plan to see Victoria Falls from both sides or make a day trip to Botswana's Chobe National Park.

faq.q: Is Zambia's safari experience different from Kenya or Tanzania?
faq.a: Yes, notably — Zambia is known for pioneering walking safaris and canoe safaris, a more intimate, slower style than the vehicle-based game drives common elsewhere.

daysReason: 8 days covers Victoria Falls, South Luangwa, and the Lower Zambezi at a good pace for walking and canoe safaris. 5–6 works if you drop one park; 10+ lets you slow the remote parks down, which suits Zambia's unhurried style.
visa: A visa on arrival (including the KAZA Univisa covering Zimbabwe too) is available for most nationalities — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Cataratas Vitória, lado da Zâmbia
attractions.desc: A margem zambiana oferece vistas mais próximas e molhadas das cataratas, incluindo o emocionante passadiço Knife-Edge Bridge, que coloca os visitantes mesmo junto à água a cair. Na época seca, a sazonal Piscina do Diabo permite nadar mesmo na borda das cataratas. Combina naturalmente com as vistas mais amplas disponíveis do lado do Zimbabué.

attractions.name: Parque Nacional do Sul de Luangwa
attractions.desc: Amplamente reconhecido como o berço do safári a pé, este parque oferece encontros próximos e guiados com leopardos, elefantes e hipopótamos ao longo do Rio Luangwa. A sua densidade de vida selvagem rivaliza com parques muito maiores e mais famosos, mas com muito menos veículos. Os passeios noturnos aqui também são bem considerados para avistar espécies noturnas.

attractions.name: Parque Nacional do Baixo Zambeze
attractions.desc: Um parque ribeirinho de frente para o Mana Pools do Zimbabué do outro lado do Zambeze, conhecido por safaris de canoa que deslizam silenciosamente por elefantes e hipopótamos junto à margem da água. A combinação de observação de vida selvagem fluvial e terrestre distingue-o de parques apenas com safaris de carro. É menos desenvolvido do que o Sul de Luangwa, atraindo viajantes que procuram uma alternativa mais tranquila.

attractions.name: Parque Nacional do Kafue
attractions.desc: Um dos maiores parques nacionais de África, ainda relativamente pouco desenvolvido para turismo, oferecendo uma verdadeira sensação de natureza selvagem. A sua dimensão sustenta habitats diversos, de planícies abertas a mata densa, com fortes populações de leões, leopardos e espécies de antílopes não encontradas em mais lado nenhum na região. O acesso requer mais planeamento do que os parques mais estabelecidos.

attractions.name: Livingstone
attractions.desc: A cidade mais próxima das Cataratas Vitória, batizada em homenagem ao explorador David Livingstone, funciona como polo de turismo de aventura do país. Bungee jumping, rafting em águas bravas e voos de microleve sobre as cataratas são todos organizados a partir daqui. O Museu de Livingstone oferece um contexto útil sobre a história colonial e pré-colonial da região.

attractions.name: Lago Kariba, margem zambiana
attractions.desc: O lado zambiano deste vasto lago artificial oferece passeios de casa-barco e lodges à beira-lago com observação de vida selvagem junto à margem. É um contraponto mais lento aos parques de safári mais intensos, com pesca e cruzeiros ao pôr do sol como atividades principais. O lago faz também fronteira com o Zimbabué, e viagens transfronteiriças são comuns.

itinerary.label: Dias 1–2
itinerary.title: Livingstone e Cataratas Vitória
itinerary.desc: Vistas próximas das cataratas mais atividades de aventura opcionais na vila.

itinerary.label: Dias 3–5
itinerary.title: Sul de Luangwa
itinerary.desc: Safaris a pé e passeios noturnos por um dos parques mais densos de vida selvagem de África.
itinerary.logistics: ~1h de voo desde Livingstone via Lusaka

itinerary.label: Dias 6–7
itinerary.title: Baixo Zambeze
itinerary.desc: Safaris de canoa ao longo do rio, deslizando por elefantes e hipopótamos.
itinerary.logistics: ~1h de voo desde o Sul de Luangwa

itinerary.label: Dia 8
itinerary.title: Lusaka
itinerary.desc: Uma pequena paragem na capital antes da partida.
itinerary.logistics: ~4h de carro ou um pequeno voo desde o Baixo Zambeze

goodToKnow.tipping: 10–15 USD/dia para guias de safári é habitual
goodToKnow.safety: As zonas turísticas são seguras e bem organizadas; a maioria das viagens é guiada
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Voos domésticos ligam Livingstone aos parques de safári; as estradas para parques remotos podem ser muito lentas
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Livingstone's Harry Mwanga Nkumbula International Airport (LVI) is the natural start for this route, right by Victoria Falls

food.name: Nshima
food.desc: Uma papa espessa de milho e o alimento base da Zâmbia, comida com um acompanhamento de carne ou legumes.

food.name: Kapenta
food.desc: Pequenos peixes secos ou frescos do Lago Kariba, uma fonte comum de proteína.

food.name: Ifisashi
food.desc: Legumes cozinhados num molho rico de amendoim.

food.name: Munkoyo
food.desc: Uma bebida tradicional fermentada e ligeiramente doce, feita de milho e raiz de munkoyo.
